Question: Which method performed the best on the GRID dataset?
Evidence:
[E1] (text, Section Table 2, page 6): Table 2: Cross-dataset evaluation of our method on GRID dataset pre-trained on LRW dataset. Methods Evaluation on GRID PSNR ↑ SSIM ↑ LMD ↓ Chung et al. [2017] 29.36 0.74 1.35 Chen et al. [2018] 29.89 0.73 1.18 Chen et al. [2019] 32.15 0.83 1.29 AMIE (Ours) 31.01 0.97 0.78
[E2] (text, Section 4.5, page 6): We conduct a user study on the LRW dataset with 42 volunteers in both realistic and synchronization of generation. We randomly select the samples generated by our method, Zhou et al. [2019] and Chen et al. [2019]. Then, the volunteers were asked to answer the following two questions: (1) which one appears more realistic and (2) which one provides more temporal synchronism referring to the ground truth. Table 4 clearly demonstrates that our model achieves the highest rating in both realistic and synchronization.
[E3] (text, Section L, page 5): 4.2 Quantitative Results We compare our model with four recent state-of-the-art methods, including Chung et al. [2017], Chen et al. [2018] Zhou et al. [2019], and Chen et al. [2019]. Table 1 shows the quantitative results of our method and its competitors with higher PSNR, SSIM and lower LMD, suggesting the best quality of the generated video frames of the talking faces. Although Zhou et al. [Zhou et al. , 2019] obtains the lowest PSNR, it obtains the second highest SSIM and its SSIM is signiﬁcantly better than Chung et al. [Chung et al. , 2017] and Chen et al. [Chen et al. , 2018]. To further verify the robustness for arbitrary person generation, we evaluate our method on another benchmark dataset GRID [Cooke et al. , 2006] and report the comparison results in Table 2. From Table 2, we observe that our model achieves the highest SSIM and the lowest LMD, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of our method. Although the PSNR of our method is a little lower than that of Chen et al. [Chen et al. , 2019], our method surpass [Chen et al. , 2019] on the metrics of both SSIM and LMD. Therefore, our method always achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM, demonstrating our method is able to generate high-quality videos.
[E4] (text, Section L, page 5): To focus on the lip movement, we only utilize the lip area of the frame for L 1 reconstruction loss, While L perc and L lip measure the distance between visual concept, it is also important to shorten the distance between audio and visual modalities in high-level representation. We implement mutual information as described before. We try to maximize it between generated frames and audios, Θ ( ˆ F, A ) . (12) Our full model is optimized according to the following objective function: 4 Experiments 4.1 Dataset and Metrics We evaluate our method on prevalent benchmark datasets LRW [Chung and Zisserman, 2016] and GRID [Cooke et al. , 2006]. Frames are aligned into 256 × 256 faces and audios are processed into (Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefﬁcient) MFCC features at the sampling rate of 5000Hz. Then we match each frame with an MFCC audio input with a size of 20 × 13 . We use common reconstruction metrics such as PSNR and SSIM [Wang et al. , 2004] to evaluate the quality of the synthesized talking faces. Furthermore, we use Landmark Distance (LMD) to evaluate the accuracy of the generated lip by calculating the landmark distance between the generated video and the original video. The lower LMD, the better of the generation.

These claims are already verified and kept:
- Our method, AMIE (Ours), achieved the highest PSNR of 31.01 on the GRID dataset.

These claims failed the checks; write corrected claims to replace them:
- "Our method, AMIE (Ours), achieved the highest SSIM of 0.97 on the GRID dataset.": support check: The evidence in E1 (Section Table 2) shows that AMIE (Ours) achieved an SSIM of 0.97 on the GRID dataset, not 0.78.
- "Our method, AMIE (Ours), achieved the lowest LMD of 0.78 on the GRID dataset.": support check: The evidence in E1 (Section Table 2) shows that AMIE (Ours) achieved an LMD of 0.78 on the GRID dataset, not the lowest LMD.
- "The paper does not explicitly state which method performed the best on the GRID dataset.": support check: The evidence in E1 (Section Table 2) shows that AMIE (Ours) achieved the highest PSNR and SSIM on the GRID dataset, and the lowest LMD. Therefore, the paper does not explicitly state which method performed the best on the GRID dataset, but it is clear that AMIE (Ours) performed better than the other methods listed.

claims.text: Our method, AMIE (Ours), achieved the highest SSIM of 0.97 on the GRID dataset.
Our method, AMIE (Ours), achieved the lowest LMD of 0.78 on the GRID dataset.
The paper does not explicitly state which method performed the best on the GRID dataset.
